note: USA targets are strategic and deliberately aggressive, Hutong NYC explicitly so, and Hutong Miami's GA4 target is derived from its Meta plan (monthly × 6738/4756). Read variance to target with that in mind. This week straddles two months, so the weekly target is pro-rata across both: three days on September and four on October, each month's GA4 target × days/30. That gives Aqua NYC 540 (2,210 × 3/30 plus 2,394 × 4/30), Hutong NYC 438 (1,575 and 2,100 on the same basis) and Hutong Miami 119 (479 and 530, both derived), 1,097 for the market against 996 last week. The USA booked 391 GA4 bookings, down 8.0 percent week on week and 64.4 percent below target. Hutong NYC has no usable last-year comparison: the site's SevenRooms tracking stopped on 22 September 2025 and did not resume until 15 October, so this week sits inside the outage window and its last-year bookings, Meta schedules and Google booking conversions are all missing. The portfolio year-on-year figure therefore sets three venues this year against two last year. Like for like, Aqua NYC and Hutong Miami booked 264 against 647, down 59.2 percent. Aqua NYC is the conversion case: users fell 15.5 percent year on year but bookings fell 65.2 percent, so conversion is 3.1 percent against 7.6 percent last year and 3.7 percent last week. Hutong Miami recovered most of last week's fall, up 25.5 percent to 69 against 79 two weeks ago with conversion at 4.3 percent against 3.6 percent last week, and Meta came down to about $36 a schedule from $54. Hutong NYC fell 17.0 percent week on week to 127 on 10.1 percent fewer users. Year to date the portfolio sits 51.2 percent behind a target that assumed growth. Google booking conversions and modelled store visits for this week are provisional and will settle upward, so read this week's paid cost per booking as a ceiling. The Google Reserve to OpenTable shift at both US Hutongs is a routing and margin change, not lost demand. The covers report carries the fuller picture.
